title: I made a Mexican Lotería (bingo) game for iPhone using a mix of AI and traditional assets.
author: noefresh
selftext:
We took the traditional Lotería characters and rebuilt them as animated 3D USDZ models using headless Blender. It includes support for iPhone Duo.

[https://apps.apple.com/us/app/lotería-book/id6820358043](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/lotería-book/id6820358043)

Workflow is basically Claude divided into two instances- one App builder, one 3D modeler and connected and coordinating with each other. Everything then plugged into Xcode and built in Swift.

This worked out great because there were 54 total cards needed to complete the traditional deck. The modeler could do them in batches of 10 and then notify the builder when it had a batch ready.

It also automated the Testflight builds so I could constantly see a WIP on my iPhone. The two instances both ran as Claude CLI in a Terminal on a Mac Studio sitting on my desk. This meant I could direct the efforts via the Claude app on my phone and easily control Xcode within being in the room or even the building.

The coder also did a pile of playtesting for me to save time. 

Time from concept to release was approximately 1 week.

We originally tried an AI-generated Spanish announcer, but it sounded kinda fake. So we found a real Mexican Lotería player to record all the calls, which turned out so much better.

It was a fun project with lots of little technical challenges along the way. Happy to answer questions about how we built it, and would love to hear what people think!

Game is released for free.
